title: Selecting DOM elements
summary: Find elements on a page with querySelector and read or change their text with textContent.

options: The first element with class mark, or null
quiz.explain: `querySelector` gives back one element, the first match in the page, or `null` if nothing matches. Use `querySelectorAll` for all matches.

quiz.q: Complete the line that finds the element whose id is `title`.
quiz.explain: The text inside `querySelector` is a CSS selector. An id selector starts with `#`.

quiz.explain: Assigning to `textContent` replaces the text inside the element, and reading it afterwards gives the new text.

quiz.q: The page has three `<li class="mark">` elements. How many items does `document.querySelectorAll('.mark')` hold?
quiz.explain: `querySelectorAll` returns a list of every match, here all 3. You can loop over it with `for...of` or `forEach`.

quiz.q: Click the line with the mistake. The goal is to set the heading text to 'Marks'.
quiz.explain: `textContent` is a property, not a function. Write `heading.textContent = 'Marks';` with no round brackets.
